## 💡 What is RAGFlow? [RAGFlow](https://ragflow.io/) is a leading open-source Retrieval-Augmented Generation ([RAG](https://ragflow.io/basics/what-is-rag)) engine that fuses cutting-edge RAG with Agent capabilities to create a superior context layer for LLMs. It offers a streamlined RAG workflow adaptable to enterprises of any scale. Powered by a converged [context engine](https://ragflow.io/basics/what-is-agent-context-engine) and pre-built agent templates, RAGFlow enables developers to transform complex data into high-fidelity, production-ready AI systems with exceptional efficiency and precision. ## 🎮 Get Started Try our cloud service at [https://cloud.ragflow.io](https://cloud.ragflow.io). For local deployment, see [Local Deployment](#-local-deployment).
## 🔥 Latest Updates - 2026-11-06 RAGFlow 1.0.0 released. - 2026-09-29 RAGFlow 1.0.0-rc1 released. - 2026-09-10 Added website content ingestion through sitemaps. - 2026-08-19 Introduced Knowledge Compilation to generate Wikis, Graphs, Trees, PageIndex, Mind Maps, Timelines, and Skills at the document and dataset levels. - 2026-08-19 Introduced Agentic RAG with Low, Medium, High, and Ultra thinking modes. - 2026-07-02 Added Google BigQuery data source ingestion and incremental synchronization. See the [full release notes](https://ragflow.io/docs/dev/release_notes) for more updates. ## 🌟 Key Features ### 🍭 **"Quality in, quality out"** - Deep document understanding-based knowledge extraction from unstructured data with complicated formats. - Finds "needle in a data haystack" of literally unlimited tokens. ### 🍱 **Template-based chunking** - Intelligent and explainable. - Plenty of template options to choose from. ### 🧩 **Knowledge Compilation** - Compile content at the document and dataset levels into structured knowledge artifacts. - Use compilation templates to generate Wikis, Graphs, Trees, PageIndex, Mind Maps, Timelines, and Skills for different knowledge organization and reuse needs. - Configure compilation models and processing rules, and view, update, and regenerate knowledge artifacts. ### 🧠 **Agentic Retrieval** - Perform multi-step retrieval for complex questions: the model analyzes the question and, when needed, breaks it down, retrieves knowledge, and verifies evidence. - Gather more complete context through multiple rounds of retrieval and reasoning to help generate well-grounded answers. - Choose Low, Medium, High, or Ultra thinking modes to control retrieval and reasoning depth according to question complexity. ### 🌱 **Grounded citations with reduced hallucinations** - Visualization of text chunking to allow human intervention. - Quick view of the key references and traceable citations to support grounded answers. ### 🍔 **Compatibility with heterogeneous data sources** - Supports Word documents, PowerPoint presentations, Excel spreadsheets, TXT files, images, PDFs, scanned copies, structured data, web pages, and more. ### 🛀 **Automated and effortless RAG workflow** - Streamlined RAG orchestration catered to both personal and large businesses. - Configurable LLMs as well as embedding models. - Multiple recall paired with fused re-ranking. - Intuitive APIs for seamless integration with business. ## 🔎 System Architecture
## 🏠 Local Deployment Local deployment supports both Docker deployment and launching from source. Docker is suitable for quick evaluation, integration testing, and production deployment, while launching from source is intended for RAGFlow development and debugging. Docker deployment does not require a Go compiler. Launching from source requires the Go version specified in `go.mod`; frontend development additionally requires Node.js and npm. ### 🐳 Docker Deployment #### 📝 Docker Deployment Prerequisites - Recommended starting configuration: 4 CPU cores, 16 GB RAM, and 50 GB of available disk space. Actual requirements depend on the document engine, data volume, parsing tasks, and concurrency. Local models and other optional components may require additional resources. - Docker ≥ 24.0.0, Docker Compose ≥ v2.26.1. > [!TIP] > If you have not installed Docker on your local machine (Windows, macOS, or Linux), see [Install Docker Engine](https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/). #### 🚀 Start up the server 1. If using Elasticsearch, set `vm.max_map_count` on the Docker host to at least 262144. This step is usually unnecessary with Infinity: > To check the value of `vm.max_map_count`: > > ```bash > sysctl vm.max_map_count > ``` > > If you use Elasticsearch and the value is below 262144, reset it: > > ```bash > # In this case, we set it to 262144: > sudo sysctl -w vm.max_map_count=262144 > ``` > > This change will be reset after a system reboot. To ensure your change remains permanent, add or update the `vm.max_map_count` value in **/etc/sysctl.conf** accordingly: > > ```bash > vm.max_map_count=262144 > ``` 2. Clone the repository: ```bash git clone https://github.com/infiniflow/ragflow.git ``` 3. Check out the release tag and start the server with Docker Compose: Enter the Docker deployment directory. ```bash cd ragflow/docker ``` Check out the `v1.0.0` release tag. ```bash git checkout v1.0.0 ``` Start the RAGFlow services and their dependencies. ```bash docker compose -f docker-compose.yml up -d ``` With the default MySQL configuration, the image entrypoint runs database migrations before starting Admin, Syncer, Ingestor, API, and other services. > In the RAGFlow open-source 1.0 release, DeepDoc uses CPU inference for layout analysis, OCR, and table recognition. 4. Check the server status after startup: Use `docker ps` to check the dependency services. After the dependencies show `healthy` and the RAGFlow container remains running, use the HTTP endpoint to determine whether RAGFlow is ready. The RAGFlow container itself does not define a Compose healthcheck. ```bash curl -f http://localhost/api/v1/system/healthz ``` After receiving an HTTP 200 response, open the Web UI. If you changed `SVR_WEB_HTTP_PORT`, replace the port in the health-check URL accordingly. If startup fails, inspect the container logs: ```bash docker logs --tail 50 ragflow-cpu ``` 5. In your web browser, enter the IP address of your server and log in to RAGFlow. > With the default settings, you only need to enter `http://IP_OF_YOUR_MACHINE` (**without** port number), because the default HTTP serving port `80` can be omitted when using the default configuration. 6. After signing in, add an LLM, embedding, and reranker on the model provider page, including the model name, service address, and API key. > For details, see [llm_api_key_setup](https://ragflow.io/docs/dev/llm_api_key_setup). _The show is on!_ See the [Quickstart guide](./docs/quickstart.mdx) for details. #### ⚙️ Docker Configuration and Adjustment Docker deployment uses `docker/.env` and `docker/docker-compose.yml`. releases.name: v1.0.0
releases.body:
After three release candidates, we are pleased to announce the official release of RAGFlow 1.0, now ready for production. Built on a complete rewrite in Go, this release significantly reduces deployment and runtime overhead and introduces an all-new Agentic Chat experience. We encourage all users to upgrade for improved stability, performance, and question answering.

### Highlights
- Rewritten in Go for lighter deployment: Docker images are approximately 10× smaller, and startup is approximately 10× faster.
- Approximately 100× greater concurrency, with substantial improvements in query latency, memory usage, and document parsing speed.
- All-new Agentic Chat: Enables multi-step reasoning and answers to complex questions through iterative retrieval, tool calls, and evidence sufficiency assessment.

### Chat and Agents
- Added Agentic Chat mode, replacing the previous Low, Medium, High, and Ultra thinking levels.
- Introduced the Jev decision model into the agent tool-calling loop to determine whether the available evidence is sufficient to answer a question.
- Added support for the Jev decision model in the Categorize agent component.
- Added storage and display of prom

1.0.0-rc3 is the third and final release candidate before the official v1.0.0 release. It fixes several issues found in rc2 and introduces new features and enhancements.

## Key updates:
1. Introduced the decision model for evidence sufficiency judgment within the agentic tool loop, and the Categorize component for agents.
2. Added support for multiple versions of ingestion pipeline DSL.
3. Chat history now stores and displays prompts, token usage, and execution time.
4. Compatible with existing v1.0.0-rc2 schema, allowing a direct upgrade.

releases.name: v1.0.0-rc2
releases.body:
1.0.0-rc2 is the second release candidate for v1.0.0. This release fixes several issues in rc1 and introduces new features and expanded support.

### Highlights
1. Introduced Agentic mode for chat, replacing the Low, Medium, High, and Ultra thinking levels.
2. Preserved compatibility with existing v1.0.0-rc1 data, allowing direct upgrades.
3. Added support for Team/Me sharing.
4. Added support for model providers DemonRoute and Opper, web search tools Firecrawl and Search1API, and the MinerU 4 model.
5. Added retrieval support for Czech and Slovak.
6. Unified the 12 built-in document parsers with the Pipeline parsers.
7. Added Docker images for the arm64 architecture.

## What's Changed
* refactor(parser): unify spreadsheet tables on a segmented HTML wire by @jay77721 in https://github.com/infiniflow/ragflow/pull/20358
* refactor: use correct ragflow.conf as nginx config file by @JinHai-CN in https://github.com/infiniflow/ragflow/pull/20321
* docs:update Docker commands in deployment guides by @Yannnnnnny in https://github.com/infiniflow/ragflow/pull/20353

💡 What is RAGFlow?

RAGFlow is a leading open-source Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) engine that fuses cutting-edge RAG with Agent capabilities to create a superior context layer for LLMs. It offers a streamlined RAG workflow adaptable to enterprises of any scale. Powered by a converged context engine and pre-built agent templates, RAGFlow enables developers to transform complex data into high-fidelity, production-ready AI systems with exceptional efficiency and precision.

🎮 Get Started

Try our cloud service at https://cloud.ragflow.io.

For local deployment, see Local Deployment.

🔥 Latest Updates

  • 2026-11-06 RAGFlow 1.0.0 released.
  • 2026-09-29 RAGFlow 1.0.0-rc1 released.
  • 2026-09-10 Added website content ingestion through sitemaps.
  • 2026-08-19 Introduced Knowledge Compilation to generate Wikis, Graphs, Trees, PageIndex, Mind Maps, Timelines, and Skills at the document and dataset levels.
  • 2026-08-19 Introduced Agentic RAG with Low, Medium, High, and Ultra thinking modes.
  • 2026-07-02 Added Google BigQuery data source ingestion and incremental synchronization.

See the full release notes for more updates.

🌟 Key Features

🍭 "Quality in, quality out"

  • Deep document understanding-based knowledge extraction from unstructured data with complicated formats.
  • Finds "needle in a data haystack" of literally unlimited tokens.

🍱 Template-based chunking

  • Intelligent and explainable.
  • Plenty of template options to choose from.

🧩 Knowledge Compilation

  • Compile content at the document and dataset levels into structured knowledge artifacts.
  • Use compilation templates to generate Wikis, Graphs, Trees, PageIndex, Mind Maps, Timelines, and Skills for different knowledge organization and reuse needs.
  • Configure compilation models and processing rules, and view, update, and regenerate knowledge artifacts.

🧠 Agentic Retrieval

  • Perform multi-step retrieval for complex questions: the model analyzes the question and, when needed, breaks it down, retrieves knowledge, and verifies evidence.
  • Gather more complete context through multiple rounds of retrieval and reasoning to help generate well-grounded answers.
  • Choose Low, Medium, High, or Ultra thinking modes to control retrieval and reasoning depth according to question complexity.

🌱 Grounded citations with reduced hallucinations

  • Visualization of text chunking to allow human intervention.
  • Quick view of the key references and traceable citations to support grounded answers.

🍔 Compatibility with heterogeneous data sources

  • Supports Word documents, PowerPoint presentations, Excel spreadsheets, TXT files, images, PDFs, scanned copies, structured data, web pages, and more.

🛀 Automated and effortless RAG workflow

  • Streamlined RAG orchestration catered to both personal and large businesses.
  • Configurable LLMs as well as embedding models.
  • Multiple recall paired with fused re-ranking.
  • Intuitive APIs for seamless integration with business.

🔎 System Architecture

🏠 Local Deployment

Local deployment supports both Docker deployment and launching from source. Docker is suitable for quick evaluation, integration testing, and production deployment, while launching from source is intended for RAGFlow development and debugging. Docker deployment does not require a Go compiler. Launching from source requires the Go version specified in go.mod; frontend development additionally requires Node.js and npm.

🐳 Docker Deployment

📝 Docker Deployment Prerequisites

  • Recommended starting configuration: 4 CPU cores, 16 GB RAM, and 50 GB of available disk space. Actual requirements depend on the document engine, data volume, parsing tasks, and concurrency. Local models and other optional components may require additional resources.
  • Docker ≥ 24.0.0, Docker Compose ≥ v2.26.1.

Tip

If you have not installed Docker on your local machine (Windows, macOS, or Linux), see Install Docker Engine.

🚀 Start up the server

  1. If using Elasticsearch, set vm.max_map_count on the Docker host to at least 262144. This step is usually unnecessary with Infinity:

    To check the value of vm.max_map_count:

    sysctl vm.max_map_count

    If you use Elasticsearch and the value is below 262144, reset it:

    # In this case, we set it to 262144:
sudo sysctl -w vm.max_map_count=262144

    This change will be reset after a system reboot. To ensure your change remains permanent, add or update the vm.max_map_count value in /etc/sysctl.conf accordingly:

    vm.max_map_count=262144

  2. Clone the repository:

    git clone https://github.com/infiniflow/ragflow.git

  3. Check out the release tag and start the server with Docker Compose:

    Enter the Docker deployment directory.

    cd ragflow/docker

    Check out the v1.0.0 release tag.

    git checkout v1.0.0

    Start the RAGFlow services and their dependencies.

    docker compose -f docker-compose.yml up -d

    With the default MySQL configuration, the image entrypoint runs database migrations before starting Admin, Syncer, Ingestor, API, and other services.

    In the RAGFlow open-source 1.0 release, DeepDoc uses CPU inference for layout analysis, OCR, and table recognition.

  4. Check the server status after startup:

    Use docker ps to check the dependency services. After the dependencies show healthy and the RAGFlow container remains running, use the HTTP endpoint to determine whether RAGFlow is ready. The RAGFlow container itself does not define a Compose healthcheck.

    curl -f http://localhost/api/v1/system/healthz

    After receiving an HTTP 200 response, open the Web UI. If you changed SVR_WEB_HTTP_PORT, replace the port in the health-check URL accordingly.

    If startup fails, inspect the container logs:

    docker logs --tail 50 ragflow-cpu

  5. In your web browser, enter the IP address of your server and log in to RAGFlow.

    With the default settings, you only need to enter http://IP_OF_YOUR_MACHINE (without port number), because the default HTTP serving port 80 can be omitted when using the default configuration.

  6. After signing in, add an LLM, embedding, and reranker on the model provider page, including the model name, service address, and API key.

    For details, see llm_api_key_setup.

    The show is on!

See the Quickstart guide for details.

⚙️ Docker Configuration and Adjustment

Docker deployment uses docker/.env and docker/docker-compose.yml. Configure the image, ports, passwords, document engine, and model image source as described in the Docker configuration guide. For platform support (note that macOS is not currently supported), see the Go Docker image build and platform support guide. To build the Docker image from source, see the Go Docker image build and platform support guide.

For document-engine changes, configuration updates, restarting services, and retaining or removing existing data, follow the Docker configuration guide.

🔨 Launch from Source

📝 Source Build Prerequisites

  1. Clone the repository and install the Go version specified in go.mod (currently Go 1.27), Clang 20, LLD 20, CMake ≥ 4.0, and PCRE2 development files. Go services depend on CGO and native static libraries; build.sh sets the required build parameters.

    git clone https://github.com/infiniflow/ragflow.git
cd ragflow

  2. Run the dependency download script once to prepare everything the local Go server needs to build, run, parse documents and count tokens (download_dev_deps.py fetches the native static libraries and the runtime resources — cl100k vocabulary, DeepDoc .ort weights, embedding tokenizer assets):

    uv run tools/scripts/download_dev_deps.py

    This is the local-dev one-stop: after one run the environment is ready, and already-present files are skipped so re-running never re-downloads. The image-facing counterpart deps/download_deps.py fetches the same runtime resources and skips the native .a files — run it only when building the dependency image or in CI, not for local development.

    download_dev_deps.py pulls and unpacks pdfium, pdf_oxide, office_oxide, and onnxruntime under ~/ragflow-native-libs, and writes the cl100k vocabulary, DeepDoc models, and embedding tokenizer assets under deps/. It is a Python script; uv run installs its declared dependencies (requests and huggingface-hub) automatically. Skip this step if you have prepared the same resources by other means. When started from the repository root, Go services automatically find internal/rag/res/deepdoc; to start from another directory, set DEEPDOC_MODEL_DIR to its absolute path.

  3. Build the services:

    ./build.sh --all

  4. Start the local dependency services and make sure the hosts and ports in conf/service_conf.yaml point to addresses accessible from the host. If using Elasticsearch, first set vm.max_map_count on the Docker host to at least 262144.

    sudo sysctl -w vm.max_map_count=262144
docker compose --env-file docker/.env -f docker/docker-compose-base.yml up -d --wait es01 mysql minio nats kvrocks

  5. Migrate the database:

    ./bin/ragflow_server --migrate

  6. Start the four services in four separate terminals:

    Terminal 1: start Admin on port 9381.

    ./bin/ragflow_server --admin
    ./bin/ragflow_server --ingestor

    Terminal 3: start Syncer.

    ./bin/ragflow_server --syncer

    Terminal 4: start API on port 9380.

    ./bin/ragflow_server --api

    The startup modes work as follows:

    • --migrate: Runs database migrations and exits when complete.
    • --admin: Starts the Admin service for management and initialization operations.
    • --ingestor: Starts the Ingestor service for data ingestion and parsing tasks.
    • --syncer: Starts the Syncer service for external data source synchronization tasks.
    • --api: Starts the API service for the Web UI and SDKs.

  7. Only when developing the frontend, install Node.js and npm, then start the React frontend:

    cd web
npm install

    After the services start, confirm that the API is ready:

    curl -f http://127.0.0.1:9380/api/v1/system/healthz

    An HTTP 200 response indicates that the API is responding. See Launch Service from Source for complete frontend and DeepDoc verification steps.

See Launch Service from Source for details.

aiSummary.oneLiner: An open-source RAG engine for enterprise that provides deep document understanding and verifiable AI responses.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: RAGFlow is an enterprise-grade Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) engine designed to deeply understand and process complex documents. It bridges the gap between large language models and highly specific corporate data by parsing text, tables, and images accurately before ingestion. The engine prioritizes explainability by providing grounded citations that trace AI answers back to the exact source paragraphs or data points. Its robust architecture allows teams to build reliable, hallucination-free question-answering systems over their proprietary knowledge bases. The architecture natively incorporates intelligent agents to dynamically route and refine complex context retrieval tasks.
keyFeatures: Deep Document Parsing: Accurately extracts content from diverse and complex formats including PDFs, Word documents, Excel sheets, and images.
Grounded Citations: Ensures every generated response is verifiable by linking back to the precise source material within the document.
Automated Chunking: Intelligently segments text to optimize the context window and retrieval performance for large language models.
Enterprise Ready Integration: Provides RESTful APIs and pre-built components for seamless embedding into existing corporate workflows and applications.
Visual Data Handling: Processes and retrieves information embedded within charts and images to provide comprehensive answers.
Explainable AI Engine: Minimizes hallucinations by strictly constraining the language model's output to the ingested and retrieved context.
Agentic Routing: Uses intelligent agents to categorize and distribute queries to the most appropriate context layers.

useCases.title: Corporate Knowledge Base Queries
useCases.description: Used by employees to query vast repositories of internal HR policies, technical manuals, and financial reports with verifiable accuracy.

useCases.title: Legal Document Analysis
useCases.description: Used by legal teams to quickly locate specific clauses or precedents within hundreds of pages of contracts and case files.

useCases.title: Customer Support Automation
useCases.description: Used by support agents to instantly retrieve exact troubleshooting steps and product specifications from complex user manuals.

useCases.title: Financial Report Extraction
useCases.description: Used by analysts to pull specific data points and contextual explanations from dense, table-heavy quarterly earnings reports.

useCases.title: Enterprise Search
useCases.description: Organizations build highly accurate internal search tools backed by agent-curated documentation indices.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: RAGFlow is for enterprise developers, data engineers, and AI architects building custom knowledge retrieval systems. It is ideal for organizations that require highly accurate, verifiable AI interactions based on their own complex documents. Users should have experience with Docker, API integration, and foundational RAG concepts.
